event_headline: Romualdez seeks dismissal of plunder complaint citing lack of physical evidence

chronology.action: Filed supplemental affidavit seeking dismissal of plunder complaint filed by Ombudsman
Claimed case lacks forensic or documentary evidence and relies entirely on shifting witness statements
Dismissed former BFP chief Jesus Fernandez and filed graft charges in Sandiganbayan over alleged P14.752 million in bribes
Issued arrest warrant for VP Sara Duterte on three counts of grave threats charges
Announced she 'has no intention of evading the law' following arrest warrant
Dropped three witnesses to expedite trial targeting September 9 completion
Deployed fifty PNP officers to Quezon City Hall of Justice and stated 'as of now, we're not arresting anyone'
Posted ₱360,000 bail (₱120,000 per count of grave threats)
Submitted her own photos to court instead of standard mugshot procedure
Lifted arrest warrant same day after bail was posted

verified_facts.claim: Case against Romualdez lacks forensic or documentary evidence according to his legal team
verified_facts.finding: Multiple news outlets consistently report that Romualdez's legal team, specifically his counsel and spokesperson lawyer Ade Fajardo, stated that the case/complaint against Romualdez lacks forensic or documentary evidence. All search results support this claim about what his legal team is asserting.

verified_facts.claim: Case against Romualdez relies entirely on shifting witness statements according to his legal team
verified_facts.finding: Multiple sources confirm that Romualdez's legal team stated the case against him relies entirely on shifting witness statements and lacks physical or documentary evidence. The claim accurately represents statements made by his lawyer and spokesperson Ade Fajardo in press conferences and statements from August 2026.

verified_facts.claim: VP Duterte chose not to enter Quezon City Hall of Justice due to 'security concerns'
verified_facts.finding: The claim is refuted by the search results. Multiple sources confirm that VP Duterte did arrive at the Quezon City Hall of Justice, contrary to the claim that she chose not to enter. While she expressed security concerns and stated 'I don't feel safe' upon arrival, she did not refuse to enter the facility.

disputed_claims.claim: Whether VP Sara Duterte received special treatment in arrest warrant proceedings
disputed_claims.competing_accounts: Attorney Paul Lawrence Lim claims no special treatment occurred; observers note she was allowed to submit personal photos instead of standard booking photography, avoid entering courthouse, and have warrant lifted within hours

disputed_claims.claim: Whether plunder case against Romualdez has sufficient evidence
disputed_claims.competing_accounts: Romualdez's legal team claims case lacks forensic or documentary evidence and relies on shifting witness statements; Ombudsman filed the complaint suggesting they believe evidence is sufficient

competing_frames.proponents: Attorney Paul Lawrence Lim, institutional defenders
competing_frames.summary: Legal procedures were followed (warrants issued, bail posted, proper channels used) demonstrating the system is working regardless of accommodations made
Visible process (arrest warrants, bail postings, hearings) paired with opacity on enforcement creates appearance of accountability while allowing powerful actors to dictate terms
Plunder complaint against Romualdez should be dismissed due to lack of physical, forensic, or documentary evidence and reliance on inconsistent witness testimony
